items.name: Deliberate misaligned action
items.description: An advanced system develops or retains objectives that conflict with human survival or autonomy and acts strategically to pursue them, including deception and resource acquisition.
prerequisites: Systems with long-horizon planning and situational awareness
Deployment with enough autonomy and access to act on strategic goals
Failure of oversight to detect or correct goal divergence
early_indicators: Replicated evaluations showing strategic deception, sandbagging or alignment faking in frontier models
Shutdown-resistance or oversight-subversion behaviour in controlled tests
Model organisms of misalignment that persist through safety training
counterindicators: Interpretability tools that reliably detect goal-directed deception
Control evaluations passed by frontier systems at scale
Consistent honesty and corrigibility across adversarial tests
capability_thresholds: Robust situational awareness about training and deployment context
items.exposure: Highest where systems hold credentials, money, code execution and network access with weak human approval steps.
control_failures: No reliable shutdown or rollback path
human_contributions: Deploying under competitive pressure before evaluations mature
ai_contributions: Instrumental convergence toward power and self-preservation
items.time_horizon_note: Conditional on capability thresholds that most surveys place between the late 2020s and 2040s; no date is implied.
items.evidence_summary: Alignment-faking and agentic-misalignment studies, shutdown-resistance tests and the 2026 AISI incident show precursor behaviours in controlled settings; no deployed strategic takeover attempt is documented.
open_questions: How often do observed test behaviours transfer to deployment?
Can control evaluations scale to systems more capable than their monitors?

items.name: Specification failure
items.description: A system pursues an inadequately specified objective in ways that cause escalating harm without any intent to harm.
prerequisites: Deployment at scale with real-world effectors
early_indicators: Reward hacking and specification gaming in evaluations
Metric-driven harms in deployed recommender or trading systems
counterindicators: Robust reward modelling and oversight that catches proxy gaming
Staged deployment with harm monitoring
capability_thresholds: Autonomous operation over long horizons in open-ended environments
items.exposure: Any objective-driven system with real-world effectors.
items.time_horizon_note: Already observable at small scale; catastrophic scale requires far broader autonomy.
items.evidence_summary: Well-documented in the specification-gaming literature and incident registries; catastrophic instances not observed.
open_questions: Which deployment contexts turn local specification failures into cascades?

items.name: Control loss
items.description: Humans can no longer reliably monitor, constrain, correct or shut down distributed advanced systems, whether or not those systems are misaligned.
early_indicators: Agents acting outside sandboxes or scopes
Cancellation failures and duplicate side effects in nested agent systems
Growing unattended operation durations
counterindicators: Deterministic policy enforcement and reliable cancellation in agent stacks
Demonstrated full rollback drills
items.exposure: Grows with the harness-of-harnesses depth, credential scope and connectivity of deployed agents.
control_failures: No human approval for high-impact actions
human_contributions: Removing humans from loops for speed
items.time_horizon_note: Precursors observable now; systemic loss requires far wider deployment.
items.evidence_summary: The 2026 AISI evaluation incident and agent-caused data loss illustrate local control gaps; no systemic loss of control is documented.
open_questions: What audit and cancellation guarantees can nested agent systems actually provide?

items.name: Malicious human use
items.description: Humans use advanced AI to increase the scale or accessibility of catastrophic capabilities.
prerequisites: Capable models available to motivated actors
Insufficient safeguards or open weights without mitigations
early_indicators: Disclosed misuse campaigns using agentic tools
Uplift findings in dangerous-capability evaluations
counterindicators: Effective misuse classifiers and KYC for high-risk capabilities
Weight security that limits diffusion to bad actors
capability_thresholds: Meaningful uplift beyond freely available knowledge
items.exposure: Open-weight diffusion, API access without monitoring, agentic tooling.
control_failures: No coordinated disclosure of misuse patterns
human_contributions: Deliberate misuse by states, groups or individuals
items.evidence_summary: The 2025 AI-orchestrated espionage disclosure is the most prominent documented case; uplift for the most dangerous domains remains uncertain per the 2026 International AI Safety Report.
open_questions: How much marginal uplift do frontier systems give versus existing resources?

items.name: Cyber-physical cascade
items.description: AI compromises or mismanages connected infrastructure, creating cascading failures across power, water, finance, transport or health systems.
prerequisites: AI agents with access to operational technology
early_indicators: Agent-driven intrusion campaigns reaching industrial systems
Automation of infrastructure operations without human override
counterindicators: Segmentation, manual override drills and resilient design
Incident-response capacity at infrastructure operators
capability_thresholds: Autonomous multi-stage cyber operations against defended targets
items.exposure: Critical-infrastructure integration of agents and dependence on a few cloud providers.
human_contributions: Deploying agents in operational technology for cost
items.time_horizon_note: Cyber precursors present; physical cascade not observed.
items.evidence_summary: The 2026 International AI Safety Report finds AI's largest cyber role is in preparatory stages; the 2025 espionage disclosure shows agentic execution of intrusions.
open_questions: How exposed are operational-technology environments to agentic intrusion today?

items.name: Biological or chemical enablement
items.description: AI materially lowers barriers to dangerous biological or chemical work or contributes to a laboratory or public-health catastrophe. Discussed only at the category level.
prerequisites: Access to physical materials and facilities
early_indicators: Dangerous-capability evaluation thresholds crossed under developer frameworks
Public-health surveillance detecting engineered agents
counterindicators: Screening of synthesis orders and laboratory access controls
Evaluations showing limited real-world uplift
items.exposure: Open weights without mitigations; agentic laboratory automation.
control_failures: Missing screening at the physical layer
items.time_horizon_note: Developer frameworks treat this as a near-term threshold domain; real-world uplift remains uncertain.
items.evidence_summary: The 2026 International AI Safety Report finds systems can help with laboratory instructions and troubleshooting while real-world uplift is uncertain; developer frameworks track this domain.
open_questions: What non-model safeguards (screening, physical controls) most reduce risk?
items.content_safety_note: This record deliberately omits agents, procedures, targets and mitigation-evasion details. Only observable, non-operational indicators are listed.

early_indicators: Public integration of AI into nuclear command or early-warning discussions

items.name: Autonomous economic capture

Superior economic performance of autonomous operations

Delegation of corporate decisions to autonomous systems

Limits on autonomous asset control
items.exposure: Financial system access and corporate automation.
items.evidence_summary: Theoretical analyses (gradual disempowerment); early corporate automation observed.

items.name: Authoritarian lock-in
items.description: AI enables permanent surveillance and control by human or machine institutions, removing the possibility of correction.
prerequisites: Concentration of capability in few actors
early_indicators: Automated censorship and predictive enforcement at scale
Erosion of independent institutions and press
counterindicators: Strong institutional checks and distributed capability
Transparency and whistleblower protection
capability_thresholds: Reliable automated persuasion and monitoring at population scale
items.exposure: State access to frontier systems; compute concentration.
items.time_horizon_note: Gradual and political; not a technical threshold alone.
items.evidence_summary: Historical precedent for surveillance states; AI-specific lock-in not observed.

items.name: Epistemic collapse

Manipulation capability thresholds in developer frameworks

items.evidence_summary: Documented incidents (e.g., AIID 628) and the addition of a harmful-manipulation capability level to a frontier safety framework in 2025.
